The Tribes and Their Advantages
The Tribes and Their Advantages
One of the first and most important decisions in Travian: Legends is choosing your tribe. Each tribe has its own unique strengths, weaknesses, and playstyle. Picking the right one will depend on whether you prefer attacking, defending, supporting allies, or growing steadily.
This guide will help you understand what each tribe offers so you can make the best choice for your journey.
Vikings (find out more about their advantages)
A fearsome new addition to Travian: Legends, the Vikings are strong raiders with powerful infantry and efficient cavalry.
Highlights:
Berserkers: Deal massive damage and always take down at least one enemy when attacking, but eat twice as much crop.
Valkyries: Heavy cavalry that only consume 2 crop per unit, making them very efficient.
Specials: Barricade (defensive bonus), fast raid ships, Jarl (reduces enemy loyalty by 15–30%), hero reduces loyalty by 5%.
Merchants: Carry 750 resources, move at 18 fields/hour.
Best for players who love aggressive raiding and efficient early attacks.
Romans (find out more about their advantages)
The most beginner-friendly tribe, Romans are versatile and strong in both attack and defense, though their units take longer and cost more to train.
Highlights:
Can build resource fields and buildings simultaneously.
Elite infantry, but weak cavalry defense.
Specials: Horse Drinking Trough (reduces cavalry crop consumption), strong city wall.
Merchants: Carry 500 resources, move at 16 fields/hour.
Senator: Reduces loyalty by 20–30%.
Hero: Gains +100 strength per point invested (instead of 80).
Best for new players who want balance and flexibility.
Gauls (find out more about their advantages)
Peace-loving but versatile, Gauls are great defenders and have the fastest units in the game. Perfect for players who want flexibility and a safer start.
Highlights:
Fastest units in Travian.
Strong defense, weaker offense.
Specials: Palisade wall, Trapper (captures enemy troops), extra-large crannies (1.5× protection).
Merchants: Carry 750 resources, move at 24 fields/hour.
Cheap settlers, but expensive siege weapons.
Chieftain: Reduces loyalty by 20–25%.
Hero: +5 speed when mounted.
Great for beginners who want defense, speed, and flexibility.
Teutons (find out more about their advantages)
The most aggressive tribe, Teutons are feared raiders with cheap, fast-produced troops and high carrying capacity.
Highlights:
Best raiders with fast and cheap troop training.
Weak discipline and slower units overall.
Specials: Brewery (increases attack power), Earth Wall (hard to destroy but weak defense).
Merchants: Carry 1000 resources, move at 12 fields/hour.
Chief: Reduces loyalty by 20–25%.
Hero: Provides a plunder bonus (20% cranny dip).
Best for offensive and experienced players who enjoy constant raiding.
Huns (find out more about their advantages)
Masters of mounted combat, the Huns are aggressive raiders with devastating cavalry but weak defenses. Recommended for experienced players.
Highlights:
Fast, powerful cavalry, but poor defensive units.
Specials: Command Center (extra expansion), weak Makeshift Wall.
Merchants: Carry 500 resources, move at 20 fields/hour.
Logades: Reduces loyalty by 15–30%.
Hero: Gives +3 speed to mounted armies.
Best for veterans who prefer aggressive raiding and expansion.
Egyptians (find out more about their advantages)
Masters of economy and defense, Egyptians are strong builders with high resource production. They can train armies quickly and cheaply.
Highlights:
Cheap and fast basic units.
Strong defensive troops and a durable Stone Wall.
Weak in offense.
Specials: Waterworks (increases oasis bonus).
Merchants: Carry 750 resources, move at 16 fields/hour.
Nomarch: Reduces loyalty by 20–25%.
Hero: Boosts resource production.
Great for both beginners and experienced players who want economic power and strong defense.
Spartans (find out more about their advantages)
A late-game powerhouse, Spartans focus on military excellence with expensive but efficient troops.
Highlights:
Very strong units, efficient in crop use.
Troops are slow and costly to train, but powerful in battle.
Specials: Asclepeion (restores up to 60% of lost troops), weak Defensive Wall.
Merchants: Carry 500 resources, move at 14 fields/hour.
Ephor: Reduces loyalty by 20–25%.
Hero: Gains +50% strength from Spartan weapons, and these weapons also buff Spartan troops.
Best for advanced players who aim for strength in the later stages of the game.
Final Tip
There is no single “best” tribe — the right choice depends on your playstyle:
New to the game? Romans or Gauls.
Love raiding? Teutons, Huns, or Vikings.
Prefer defense and economy? Egyptians or Gauls.
Long-term dominance? Spartans.
Take your time exploring each tribe — every choice will change your Travian journey!

Guide: The Marketplace - Trading Resources
Guide: The Marketplace - Trading Resources
The Marketplace is the building that enables trade. It allows you to send resources to other players, create trade offers, accept incoming offers and monitor all resource transfers. Whether you are supporting an ally, diversifying your resource income, or recovering from a deficit, the Marketplace is an essential tool throughout the game.
How Merchants Work
Merchants physically carry resources between villages. They live in your Marketplace and are dispatched whenever you send resources. Each merchant may carry a specific amount of resources, and depending on the amount you want to send, you will need one or more merchants to make the delivery.
Merchants are added automatically as you upgrade your Marketplace — you do not train them like troops.
You get one merchant per level of Marketplace.
After completing a trade, merchants travel to the destination and return home automatically.
While merchants are away, they cannot be used for another trade.
Merchants do not fight and cannot be lost, except if Marketplace is demolished or its level is lowered. Even in such case the ongoing deliveries will be finished.
Initial merchants capacity is determined by tribe. It may be upgraded by building and upgrading Trade Office, and by the Commerce alliance bonus.
Merchants speed depend on their tribe.
Tribe Differences
Each tribe has merchants with different carrying capacities. Both the initial capacity and the speed of merchants is determined by their tribe. Additionally Romans have a bonus for their Trade Office. It is twice as effective as the same building for other tribes, increasing their merchants capacity even more.
Sending Resources
How to Send Resources
Sending resources to another player is straightforward:
Open your Marketplace
Select 'Send Resources'
Enter the destination coordinates or village name
Enter how much of each resource you want to send
Confirm the trade — your merchants will depart immediately
Alternatively, you can find the target village on the map, and send the resources directly from there.
You can send any combination of the four resources in a single trip, as long as the total does not exceed your available merchants capacity. The game will automatically assign as many merchants as required for the selected amount of resources.
Travel Time
Merchants travel at their own speed. The further the destination, the longer the journey. The game shows you the estimated arrival time before you confirm — always check this when time-sensitive deliveries matter, such as sending crop to an ally under starvation pressure. 
Resources in transit cannot be stolen. If your village is attacked while your merchants are away, only the resources still in the village are at risk, including any open trade offers you made, until they are accepted. Likewise, resources being sent to you are safe until they arrive.
Sending Resources Within Your Alliance
Sending resources to alliance members is one of the most important cooperative mechanics in the game. Coordinating resource flows — such as directing crop to a player under attack, who has to feed a lot of reinforcements — is how organised alliances gain a competitive edge.
Be aware that automatic resource-sharing limits exist to prevent unfair pushing between players. Refer to the Automatic Resource-Sharing Limits article for details on how these work.
Trade Offers
Creating an Offer
Instead of sending resources directly, you can create a trade offer on the open market. This allows other players to browse available offers and accept ones that suit them:
Open the Marketplace and its 'Offer' tab
Select 'Create Offer'
Specify what resource you are offering and in what quantity
Specify what resource and quantity you want in return
Optionally limit the offer to a maximum travel time from your village or to your alliance
Confirm — your merchants are reserved and will execute the trade when someone accepts
While your offer is active, the merchants assigned to it are unavailable for other trades. You may cancel the offer at any time, until it is accepted by someone.
Accepting an Offer
You can browse trade offers from other players in the 'Buy' tab in your Marketplace. Each offer shows what is being offered, what is requested, and the exchange rate. When you find an offer you want to accept:
Review the exchange rate — check whether it is fair value for your current needs
Confirm acceptance — your merchants depart with the resources requested by the other player, and the merchants of the other player depart with the resources you wanted at the same time. Their speed might be different, so you may receive your resources earlier or later than the other player.
Trade offers are visible to all players, unless limited by the travel time or the “alliance” option.
The NPC Merchant
The NPC Merchant is a premium feature that allows you to exchange your own resources with the game itself, rather than with other players. It converts one or more of your resources into another at a fixed rate, bypassing the need to find a trading partner.
This is particularly useful when your warehouse or granary is about to be fully filled and you don’t want the resources to be wasted — for example, if you produce much more crop than other resources, and your army cannot consume all of it, so you need to regularly exchange crop into other resources to use them to upgrade buildings and train new units. The NPC Merchant acts instantly, without requiring merchants to travel.

Alliance Bonuses
Alliance Bonuses
Alliance bonuses allow alliance members to collectively improve important game mechanics by donating resources. Once unlocked, bonuses apply to all alliance members, with some limitations for newly joined players. This article explains how alliance bonuses work, what effects they provide, how to unlock them, and which exceptions apply.
Overview of Alliance Bonuses
Alliances can unlock four different bonuses. Each bonus has five levels, and higher levels increase the effect of that bonus.
The available alliance bonuses are:
Recruitment
Increases troop production speed in all troop-producing buildings
Philosophy
Increases Culture Point (CP) production
CP is generated by buildings and hero helmets
Town Hall celebrations are not affected, except on specific special servers
Metallurgy
Increases troop offensive and defensive strength
This bonus is applied on top of existing smithy upgrades
Commerce
Increases merchant carrying capacity
Special Server Exceptions
On some special servers, alliance bonuses behave differently.
Annual Special 2024 / Northern Legends
Philosophy bonus also affects Town Hall celebrations and artworks
The CP limit from these sources is increased
Commerce bonus increases merchant speed in addition to carrying capacity
Bonus Levels and Effects
Each bonus increases gradually with its level. The effects are identical across all four bonus types.

(The exact percentage depends on the bonus type.)
Unlocking Alliance Bonuses
Alliance bonuses are unlocked through resource donations from alliance members.
Key rules:
Each bonus level requires a higher total amount of resources
All four bonuses have the same resource requirements and upgrade times
Resource type does not matter; only the total amount donated is counted
Resources cannot be donated while a level is actively unlocking
Once the required amount is reached, the upgrade countdown begins automatically.

* Upgrade time and donation limits are adjusted by server speed.
Donation Limits
Each player has a daily donation limit
The limit depends on the highest bonus level currently unlocked in the alliance
Donation limits cannot be exceeded
For 3 Gold, players can triple a donation (e.g. 10,000 counts as 30,000), but this still cannot exceed the daily donation limit.
Interaction With Other Game Mechanics
Some alliance bonuses are multiplied with other effects:
Recruitment bonus is multiplied with hero items (e.g. Helmet of the Mercenary)
Metallurgy bonus is multiplied with smithy upgrades
Commerce bonus is multiplied with the Trade Office
Commerce Example
Gaul merchant base capacity: 750
Level 4 Commerce bonus (120%): 750 × 2.2 = 1,650
Level 20 Trade Office (400%): 750 × 5 = 3,750
Combined effect: 750 × 2.2 × 5 = 8,250
Daily Quests and Alliance Bonuses
Alliance contributions are part of daily quests.
While the last alliance bonus is unlocking, the daily quest cannot be completed
Once all alliance bonuses finish activating, the daily quest is automatically marked as completed for all alliance members each day
Availability for Newly Joined Players
Alliance bonuses are not fully available immediately to new members.

Gold Feature: Production Bonuses
Production bonuses are premium features that temporarily boost your resource output.They can be found in the Gold Store under the Advantages tab.
Activation and Duration
Each production bonus costs 5 Gold and increases the selected resource’s production by 25%.
The duration depends on the server speed:
7 days on 1x speed servers
3 days on 3x speed servers
Once activated, you can also enable the auto-extend option to renew the bonus automatically when it expires.
You can purchase these bonuses directly from the Gold Store or from your Village Overview.
Available Bonuses
You can activate a 25% bonus for each resource type:
Lumber
Clay
Iron
Crop
The +25% boost applies to the total production of the selected resource, not just the base rate.

Oasis
Oasis Types and Bonuses
An oasis is a special tile on the map that can be conquered by your hero and annexed to a nearby village, granting that village a permanent resource production bonus. Each village can control up to three oases, making them one of the most important long-term investments in the game.
Overview
At the beginning of the game, oases are occupied by wild animals and do not produce any resources. Resource production only starts once Beginner Protection ends. You can check the number of animals in an oasis without scouting by hovering over it or clicking it on the map. Defeating the animals rewards your hero with a bounty. The hero does You can check the number of animals in an oasis without scouting by hovering over it or clicking it on the map. Defeating the animals rewards your hero with a bounty. The hero does not need to survive the attack for this reward to be granted. Oases on the map also show: 
The type of resource bonus they provide
Whether they are free or already conquered by another player
Oasis Types and Bonuses
Each resource type has up to three kinds of oases: 
Type 1: Produces only one resource at +25% (e.g., +25% lumber, clay, iron, or crop).
Type 2: Produces one resource at +25% plus an additional +25% crop.
Type 3: Produces only one resource at +50%. Exclusive to the grey Natarian area — the zone around the World Wonder in the centre of the map, controlled by the Natar NPC faction. Available for lumber, clay, and iron only; crop oases do not have a Type 3. 
When you conquer an oasis, it grants a production bonus to the village your hero conquered it from. This bonus applies only to that village's base production. Cleopatra’s governor production bonus is also calculated from the settlement’s base production and added on top. You must have at least one oasis slot free to receive it; if all three slots are occupied, abilities 1 and 3 provide no bonus.
Production values below are at 1x game speed, when the oasis is not occupied.

* Type 3 oases are only found in the grey Natarian area near the World Wonder. They cannot be conquered by regular villages — only villages within 3 tiles of a Type 3 oasis can attempt to annex them.
Conquering Natural Oases
To conquer an oasis, it must be within 3 tiles of your village. Your Hero's Mansion must be at the required level to hold the number of oases you want:
Hero's Mansion Level 10 → 1 oasis
Hero's Mansion Level 15 → 2 oases
Hero's Mansion Level 20 → 3 oases
Your hero must attack the oasis repeatedly until it is annexed by the village they attacked from. Each attack reduces the oasis's loyalty. When loyalty reaches 0%, the oasis is conquered. An oasis also has a base defence based on a population of 500, which can kill settlers even when no Nature troops are shown. Do not attack or raid an oasis with settlers alone.
 | | 
To take an oasis from another player:
Destroy their defense
Attack with your hero the required number of times (see table below)
The number of attacks needed depends on how many oases the defender currently owns. Each hero attack reduces loyalty by a fixed percentage — and that percentage is higher when the defender owns more oases. This means taking one oasis from a player who owns three requires only a single attack, while taking the last oasis from a player who owns only one requires three attacks.
Defender owns…

 |

 | 1 attack
 |

 | 2 attacks
 | 
1 oasis
 | 3 attacks
 | 
Heroes do not disappear after conquering an oasis.
Raiding Oases
Raiding a player-owned oasis allows your troops to steal up to 10% of the resources stored in that oasis. Oasis resources regenerate fully over 10 minutes.
If you raid the same oasis again before it has fully regenerated (e.g., 7 minutes later), you only take the portion that has regenerated so far — in this example, 7%. Raiding your own oasis results in 0 net gain, because the resources stored there were produced by your own village and are simply being moved back to it.
Oasis Loyalty
Oasis loyalty is a value between 0% and 100% that reflects how firmly an oasis is held. When your hero attacks an oasis, its loyalty drops. When loyalty reaches 0%, the oasis is conquered by your village.
After being conquered, an oasis's loyalty starts regenerating automatically at 1% every 30 minutes. Players cannot influence this rate. A freshly conquered oasis with low loyalty can be retaken quickly — allow time for loyalty to rebuild if you are in a contested area.
Releasing an Oasis
To release an oasis you own:
Open the Hero's Mansion
Click the red cross next to the oasis
The oasis is released back to nature and must be captured and attached again afterward.
Release time:
~2 hours on 3x speed
~6 hours on 1x speed
If your village is conquered, all its oases are automatically released — even if you later recapture the village.

Vikings in Travian: Legends
Vikings in Travian: Legends
The Vikings are fierce warriors, explorers, and conquerors — bringing their own unique structures, hero abilities, and unit traits to Travian: Northern Legends. This guide covers everything you need to know about their special abilities, buildings, hero features, and army composition.
Viking Special Abilities and Buildings
Viking Harbor
The Viking Harbor serves as the heart of their expansion — enabling faster and more efficient raids across the seas.
Viking ships travel 24 fields per hour through deep water (on x1 worlds), faster than the 18 fields per hour of other tribes.
This speed bonus applies to raids only (not attacks or reinforcements).
Construction costs and other details are identical to regular harbors.
The Barricade
The Barricade is the Vikings’ defensive wall — solid but not their strongest feature, as Vikings prefer attacking.
Base defense: 6 points per level
Durability: 3
Defensive bonus: +1.5% per level
Building cost: 110 Wood, 170 Clay, 70 Iron, 50 Crop
Even though the Vikings are primarily offensive, a few Barricade levels can provide valuable defense for key villages.
Merchants and Trade Ships
Vikings are not just raiders — their merchants ensure a steady flow of resources between settlements.

Viking Hero
Hero Ability
The Viking hero is a powerful leader, capable of turning the tide in conquest.
When leading attacks or raids, the hero inflicts +5% loyalty damage on enemy villages.
This bonus can increase by 5 points with your own great celebrations or decrease by 5 points if the defender hosts one.
Standard conquest rules still apply — including same alliance limits, NAPs, capital restrictions, and the need for a chief or Jarl to complete the takeover.
The Viking hero’s loyalty damage applies before any administrator’s effect, but the hero cannot conquer a village alone (even at 0% loyalty).

The Jarl
Jarls are Viking leaders and administrators who command with both wisdom and authority.They are responsible for conquering new villages and expanding your empire.
Loyalty Reduction: 15–30%
Research Cost: 18,250 Wood / 13,320 Clay / 20,040 Iron / 16,480 Crop
Research Time: 5:23:45
Their presence inspires troops and ensures conquered lands integrate smoothly into your kingdom.
The Berserker’s Unique Ability: Damage on Death
Berserkers are deadly attackers who continue to harm enemies even in death.
Ability:Each Berserker killed while attacking or raiding (not defending) kills 1 enemy unit in return.
Walls and Watchtower bonuses do not reduce this effect.
The ability is calculated after the main battle results.
Wounded units still go to the hospital normally.
Formula:Surviving defenders (each type) × (Killed Berserkers ÷ Total surviving defenders)
Example:If 100 Berserkers die while attacking, and 200 Slave Militias + 100 Druidriders survive:
Total defenders: 300
100 ÷ 300 = 0.333
Effect:
200 × 0.333 = 67 Slave Militias die additionally
100 × 0.333 = 33 Druidriders die additionally
Summary
The Vikings combine speed, power, and ferocity, making them a formidable tribe for aggressive players.
Fast raids via their unique harbor system
Devastating offense with Berserkers and their death damage
Powerful hero capable of extra loyalty reduction
Strong economic logistics through enhanced trade ships
While their defenses are modest, their offensive and naval advantages make the Vikings ideal for players who prefer fast-paced, high-impact gameplay.

The Spartans and Their Advantages
The Spartans and Their Advantages
The Spartans are renowned for their military-focused society, where warfare is a way of life. From early childhood, Spartans are trained in combat and discipline — their entire culture revolves around strength, endurance, and unity on the battlefield.
While they can construct defensive walls, Spartans rely primarily on their elite troops for protection. Their soldiers are powerful, efficient, and resilient, making them exceptional in the late game, when resources and troop quality matter most.
Training Spartan units takes time and investment, but their crop efficiency and combat strength make them a formidable force once their armies are built.
The Spartans are best suited for experienced or patient players who prefer a long-term, strategic approach and powerful endgame armies.
Playstyle Tips
Focus on late-game development — Spartan troops are expensive and slow to train, but incredibly strong once ready.
Maintain steady resource production early on to support high training costs later.
Use your Asclepeion to recover troops efficiently after battles.
Combine offensive and defensive tactics — Spartans can adapt to both roles with proper planning.
Special Features
Elite Troops
 | Extremely strong units that take longer to train and cost more resources.
 | 
Efficient Crop Usage
 | Units are stronger than other tribes’ but consume the same crop amount.
 | 
Defensive Wall
 | Provides only a minor defensive bonus compared to other tribes.
 | 
Merchants
 | Can carry 500 resources (speed: 14 fields/hour).
 | 
Ephor
 | The Spartan administrator; lowers enemy village loyalty by 20–25%.
 | 
Special Building – Asclepeion
 | Functions like a Hospital, but can restore 60% of troops lost in battle. Hospital and Asclepeion 
 | 
Hero Bonus
 | Gains +50% additional fighting strength from Spartan weapons, which also boost bonuses to Spartan units. Hero Right-Hand Items 
 | 
Strategy Summary
Strengths: Very strong and efficient troops, powerful late-game potential, troop restoration advantage.Weaknesses: Slow training times, expensive units, and weak defensive wall.
If you enjoy building a disciplined and unstoppable military force that dominates the late game, the Spartans are your ideal choice.
